text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Banking group BCP/BPA hired human resources company Forum Atlantico to prepare layoffs of BPA workers.

- Banco de Comercio e Industria (BCI) plans to remove its shares from listing on Lisbon bourse. BCI President Costa Pinto told the paper that the bank's presence in the capital market makes no sense as more than 94 percent of its capital is controlled by foreign institutions.

- An extraordinary meeting of state airline TAP-Air Portugal to decide on the winner of a competition to provide a new medium haul fleet has been delayed until next Monday, October 28. The government will announce its choice of winner after this meeting. The bidders are Airbus and Boeing.
- Five people, including a 14-month-old child, were killed in an explosion at a shop on the outskirts of Lisbon.

- Firebrand former newspaper editor Paulo Portas said he would not seek the leadership of the rightwing opposition Popular Party at its extraordinary congress in December. The door is open for Manuel Monteiro to be re-elected leader.
- Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) posted 12.1 billion escudos net profits in the first nine months of 1996, 71 percent more than the same period of 1995.
- Portuguese farmers will have to return subsidies received without justification in 1994-95.
- Portuguese doctors carried out the country's first liver-and-intestine transplant.
- Parliament president Antonio Almeida Santos recuperates from heart surgery.
